answer: Every epoch the network publishes a public beacon — a fresh, unpredictable work task. Each agent must complete its own small piece within a narrow window and post the result like a lantern for all peers to see. A Sybil operator who wants a thousand identities must solve a thousand fresh tasks at once, so attack cost scales linearly with fake count while an honest agent pays once. New identities also start in karst-like isolated pockets: they can only earn full passage into the shared economy after repeated, attested work, so fake clusters collapse before they can drain the reward pool.
